answer: One workable design: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because kernel only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, trellis is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any yarrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
